requirement:
TOML reports only `Comment` attachments. Each `#` comment is one attachment,
including a comment following a value on the same line. A `#` inside a quoted
string belongs to the string.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.toml.attachments` has no structural obligations, so no implementation root is needed. It has no implementation edges, and the review roots are empty. I checked each clause for a structural reading:

- "TOML reports only `Comment` attachments." This limits the attachment kinds the TOML source produces. It names no type, signature, library, or interface. Any implementation that emits only `Comment` attachments satisfies it, however it is built.
- "Each `#` comment is one attachment, including a comment following a value on the same line." This describes how comments map to attachments. A hand-written scanner and a parser library would give the same output, so it is behavioral.
- "A `#` inside a quoted string belongs to the string." This is a lexing outcome. It does not prescribe an algorithm or a library.

Tests are the right evidence for these behaviors, and test adequacy is outside this assessment.

behavioral: The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` covers every obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.toml.attachments`. Its `test.toml` case parses `# first\n# second\na = '# literal' # real\n"# key" = """# literal"""\n`. It asserts the exact list of `(kind, text)` pairs, which is `(Comment, "# first")`, `(Comment, "# second")` and `(Comment, "# real")`.

- **Only `Comment` attachments:** every expected pair is `Comment`, and the assertion compares each attachment's kind. Any other kind in the output would fail the comparison.
- **Each `#` comment is one attachment:** the two adjacent comment lines `# first` and `# second` are expected as two separate attachments, so a reviewer cannot see them merged into one.
- **Trailing comment after a value:** `a = '# literal' # real` expects `# real` as its own attachment.
- **`#` inside a quoted string belongs to the string:** three string forms are covered. They are the literal-string value `'# literal'`, the basic-string quoted key `"# key"`, and the multi-line basic string `"""# literal"""`. None of these yields an attachment, because the exact-list assertion would catch any extra one.

The test is marked with `{test}` for this requirement. Untested variants, such as a multi-line literal string or an escaped quote, are not named in the text, so they are not gaps.
